title: Adic formal smoothness over a field implies regular locality
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra which is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and local, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. If $k\to A$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), statement and proof, lines 9534–9589 in the locally read Stacks source

proof.text: Let $k_0$ be the prime subfield of $k$. In characteristic zero, $k_0=\mathbf Q$ and [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-formally-smooth] gives the square-zero lifting property for $k_0\to k$; in characteristic $p>0$, $k_0=\mathbf F_p$ and [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] gives it with $N=2$. Apply these lifts to the $k_0$-algebra map $k\to D/J$ induced by any $k_0$-algebra map $g:A\to D/J$ that kills some $\mathfrak m^q$, where $J^2=0$: obtain a compatible map $k\to D$. Regard $D$ as a $k$-algebra through this lift and apply the given $\mathfrak m$-adic formal smoothness of $k\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] to lift $g$ to $A\to D$. The result is a $k_0$-algebra lift. Thus $k_0\to A$ has the same adic lifting property. This spells out the composition argument in the source, including the continuity condition $g(\mathfrak m^q)=0$; a lift kills $\mathfrak m^{2q}$ since $J^2=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), lines 9542-9547; Algebra Lemma Tag 0320 (lemma-formally-smooth-extensions-easy), part (3), and More on Algebra Lemmas Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth), part (1), and Tag 07EF (lemma-compose-formally-smooth)

proof.text: Let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_r A/\mathfrak m^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion], the adic formal smoothness of $k_0\to A$ from Step 1 passes to $k_0\to\widehat A$. If $\widehat A$ is regular local, so is $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local]. Hence replace $A$ by $\widehat A$ and assume it is complete. Its residue field $K=A/\mathfrak m$ has the same characteristic as $k_0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), lines 9549-9557; Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists], $A$ contains a coefficient field mapping isomorphically to $K$: its coefficient ring $\Lambda$ has maximal ideal $p\Lambda=0$ because $A$ has equal characteristic $0$ or $p$. Identify this field with $K$. The maps $k_0\to K\to A$ and $k_0\to A$ agree, since a map from the prime field is unique. Choose $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathfrak m$ whose classes form a $K$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$; such a finite basis exists because $A$ is Noetherian. Put $T=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $T$ is complete regular local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ and $\dim T=n$. Since $K\subset A$ maps isomorphically onto $A/\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak m^2=0$ in $A/\mathfrak m^2$, every class there is uniquely a constant from $K$ plus a $K$-linear combination of the classes of the $x_i$; products of two latter terms vanish. The same holds for $T/\mathfrak n^2$ with the $X_i$. Thus $x_i\mapsto X_i$ and the identity on $K$ give a local $K$-algebra isomorphism $A/\mathfrak m^2\cong T/\mathfrak n^2$. Compose with $A\to A/\mathfrak m^2$ to obtain $f_1:A\to T/\mathfrak n^2$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), lines 9557-9574; Algebra Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), part (1)

proof.text: For $r\ge1$, the quotient $T/\mathfrak n^{r+2}\to T/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ has square-zero kernel $\mathfrak n^{r+1}/\mathfrak n^{r+2}$: its square lies in $\mathfrak n^{2r+2}\subseteq\mathfrak n^{r+2}$. Starting with $f_1$, use the adic lifting property of $k_0\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] successively to obtain compatible $k_0$-algebra maps $f_r:A\to T/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$. Indeed, $f_1(\mathfrak m^2)=0$, and any lift of $f_r$ sends $\mathfrak m^{2q}$ to zero when $f_r(\mathfrak m^q)=0$; hence every $f_r$ is continuous for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology and qualifies for the next lift. Compatibility and $T=\varprojlim_rT/\mathfrak n^r$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] give a $k_0$-algebra map $f:A\to T$ reducing to $f_1$ modulo $\mathfrak n^2$. It is local, induces the identity on residue field $K$, and sends $x_i$ to $X_i$ modulo $\mathfrak n^2$. The maps $f_r$ need not be $K$-linear; only their reductions modulo $\mathfrak n^2$ were prescribed as $K$-linear.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), lines 9574-9584

proof.text: The elements $f(x_i)$ form a basis of $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$, so they generate $\mathfrak n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators]. To show $f$ is surjective, fix $t\in T$. Since $A/\mathfrak m\cong T/\mathfrak n=K$, choose $a_0\in A$ with $t-f(a_0)\in\mathfrak n$. Inductively, if $t-f(a_0+\cdots+a_{r-1})\in\mathfrak n^r$, write its class modulo $\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ as a sum of degree-$r$ monomials in the $f(x_i)$ with coefficients in $K$; lift each coefficient to an element of $A$, and take their corresponding polynomial in the $x_i$ as $a_r\in\mathfrak m^r$. Then $t-f(a_0+\cdots+a_r)\in\mathfrak n^{r+1}$. The partial sums are Cauchy in the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology; completeness of $A$ gives $a=\sum_{r\ge0}a_r\in A$. For every $r$, $f(a)$ and $t$ agree modulo $\mathfrak n^{r+1}$; the $\mathfrak n$-adic separatedness of $T$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] implies $f(a)=t$. Thus $f$ is surjective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), lines 9581-9588; the source says the surjectivity follows from completeness, with the successive approximation written out here

proof.text: A surjection $f:A\to T$ gives $\dim A\ge\dim T=n$: a strict chain of prime ideals of $T$ pulls back to a strict chain in $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], the chosen $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ generate $\mathfrak m$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators] gives $\dim A\le n$. Hence $\dim A=n$ and $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $\dim A$ elements. The definition [def-weil-regular-scheme] makes $A$ regular local; by Step 2 the original local ring is regular local as well.
